output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went up and the ladder did not. Ennu had knotted it that spring from goat gut and whale-rib rungs, and it hung from the cliff-nail like a line off a drying rack. Aun went down it, because he was Aun and wanted to see the bottom. The rungs went on past the last gull, into the Unflown, where there is no water to land on. Hesk counted the rungs and did not like the number. Tavo came by laughing and shook the ladder, and it has been knocking since. Some say Aun is still climbing down, one hand under the other. The sailors of the Leeward Reach will not put a boat under it. If you hear a rung knock on a still night, that is not the wind. That is someone who has not reached the bottom yet.
output.verse:
Rope goes down past gulls
into dark where no sea lies
someone's hand still climbs
